Question B-008-002-002.

Why the correct answer is right: A plug-in telephone radio-frequency interference (RFI) filter installed close to the affected telephone keeps RF out of the device. The properly operating amateur station can remain unchanged.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Ground and shield the telephone distribution amplifier": Most nearby telephone interference complaints are at the device or its cord; a distribution amplifier may not even be part of the installation.
- sourceIndex 2: "Stop transmitting whenever the telephone is in use": Stopping operation whenever the phone is used is not the normal cure when the amateur station is operating properly and filtering can be applied.
- sourceIndex 3: "Make internal adjustments to the telephone equipment": Internal telephone adjustments should not be the first answer; use an appropriate external RFI filter near the telephone equipment.
